prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: What Is the Comet’s Tail?; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: Illustrative comet in space, one body per scene. One irregular charcoal-gray icy center; only the broad pale dust tail is depicted and discussed. This is a selective view of a dust tail, not a claim that no other tail type exists. Sun stays to the left; dust tail is gently curved generally away from it. No flames or atmosphere like a planet.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): One irregular dark comet center containing ice and dust; One faint cloud of released dust and gas near the center; One broad pale gently curved dust tail; A distant Sun, no face; sparse stars
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: Opening near-Sun view; one comet and one visible dust tail; diffuse material, not a solid spike.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: A broad pale dust tail stretches from a much smaller irregular dark center. A distant Sun is visible left of frame. Continuity: Opening near-Sun view; one comet and one visible dust tail; diffuse material, not a solid spike.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions.
Reference emphasis: draw irregular two-lobed dark icy nucleus in two unobscured matching views, no face, and a single compact location key with distant round Sun fully inside LEFT edge, nucleus center-left and pale gently curving diffuse dust tail extending RIGHT. Stars simple little points, no dramatic flare or burning; do not outline the tail with a solid edge.

visualReview.note: Consistent two-lobed dark nucleus, diffuse dust tail away from left Sun, no flames or solid tail edge; clear scale relationship. Native source and installed WebP directly inspected.
